name: How much floor slope does a walk-in shower need?

mainEntity.name: How much slope should a walk-in shower floor have so water drains properly without feeling uncomfortable underfoot?
mainEntity.text: How much slope should a walk-in shower floor have so water drains properly without feeling uncomfortable underfoot?

acceptedAnswer.text: A walk-in shower needs a carefully designed slope so water moves toward the drain instead of collecting near the entry or along the walls. The slope should be subtle enough to feel comfortable underfoot but strong enough to keep the surface draining correctly during daily use. In practical terms, the floor must be pitched evenly and planned around the drain style, shower size, and whether the shower is curbless or has a low threshold. Too little slope leads to puddling, mildew, and water escaping into the bathroom. Too much slope can feel awkward and make standing less comfortable. The exact build approach depends on tile size, pan design, and subfloor conditions, so the floor profile should be engineered before tile is installed. This is one of the most important parts of the project because even expensive tile and fixtures will not perform well if the slope is wrong.
acceptedAnswer.description: A walk-in shower floor needs enough slope to move water to the drain without pooling, usually around 1/4 inch per foot in typical shower builds. The slope must be consistent across the shower floor and carefully balanced so the entry stays comfortable while the water still drains efficiently. Poor slope causes standing water and leaks.
